However, the full results of this study are yet to be published. • Fluoride has a direct anabolic effect on the osteoblast, stimulating bone formation; it has been given as sodium fluoride or sodium monofluorophosphate in the treat- ment of osteoporosis.3,35 However, increases in lumbar BMD with fluoride have not resulted in decreased ver- tebral fracture rate, and may even be associated with in- creased bone fragility and an increase in non-vertebral fractures.3,36 Thus fluoride is not widely recommended for osteoporosis management; fluoride water concentra- tions should be taken into account if it is used.3 • Parathyroid hormone and its analogue teriparatide also have anabolic effects on bone, and increase BMD at the spine.20,21 Daily subcutaneous injections of teriparatide reduced the risk of vertebral and non-vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.4,35 Teri- paratide has also been shown to increase lumbar and femoral BMD, and reduce non-vertebral fractures to a greater extent than alendronate.5 The response to parath- yroid hormone may be modified by previous or concur- rent treatment with antiresorptive drugs.8 Combination therapy with alendronate offered no advantage over par- athyroid hormone (or teriparatide) monotherapy in terms of changes in BMD. However, after 1 year of par- athyroid hormone monotherapy, BMD gains were maintained or increased when followed with alendro- nate therapy, but lost if followed by placebo.37 NICE recommends teriparatide as an option for the secondary prevention of osteoporotic fragility fractures in women aged 65 years and older who have had an unsatisfactory response to bisphosphonates or who are intolerant to bis- phosphonates, and who have an extremely low BMD (4 standard deviations or more below the mean) or a very low BMD (3 standard deviations or more) plus one or more additional risk factors.27 • Strontium ranelate has both anabolic and resorptive properties.17 It has been found to increase BMD at the spine and hip, and reduce new vertebral, non-vertebral, and hip fractures in postmenopausal women with oste- oporosis.9,11 • Anabolic steroids such as nandrolone have been found to increase BMD similarly to HRT, but adverse effects and limited data on fracture reduction efficacy have lim- ited their use.3,16 • There is some suggestion that HMG-CoA reductase in- hibitors (statins) can stimulate bone formation and have the potential to reduce fracture risk, but data are conflict- ing, and further trials are needed.35,38,39 • Thiazide diuretics reduce urinary calcium excretion and observational studies have found patients to have a higher BMD and few
